_about: Portal fantasy: outsiders who cross into another world, what they owe on arrival, and the choice between worlds. Story axes for story_gen.py. Each axis is rolled on its own; an entry is a string (weight 1) or {v, w, decay}. All text is our own.

crossing: a freight elevator with a floor below the basement
a flooded underpass reflected in a dry shop window
a night bus that stops at a second dawn
a borrowed coat with a door sewn into its lining
a footbridge appearing on a printed map one fold at a time
a community theater trapdoor opened during a rehearsal
a laundromat dryer that turns to show a different sky
a stairwell that descends into somebody else's childhood
arrival: a market where the stalls can sail away at noon
a salt orchard whose fruit lights a whole courtyard
a hillside town packing its houses onto sleds
a station where conductors carry their own rails
a low-tide library with stairs cut into the seabed
a public bath built beneath an upside-down waterfall
a stadium converted into a garden of glass trees
a cliff village lowering its kitchens by rope for supper
local_rule: a public promise carries the speaker's shadow as collateral
a stranger may ask three directions before owing one in return
a guest who accepts a blanket can speak for the household at dawn
a road remembers the last name spoken at its first mile
a table set for a visitor stays warm until they arrive
a doorway opens only after each side has offered a greeting
a bell rung in apology returns the last thing freely given
a story told twice in public earns its subject a seat at council
first_ally: a cartographer who has mapped every road except their own street
a ferry cook who offers a meal in exchange for news of home
a tailor mending banners from a dissolved neighborhood
a guide whose family counts each rescue as an adoption
a customs clerk keeping a private ledger of the displaced
a retired courier who knows the names of disused gates
a street musician whose audience includes homesick ghosts
a market child saving coins for an adult-sized ticket
return_anchor: a receipt from home with a second address appearing in the ink
a key that warms whenever someone at home asks after its owner
a snapshot whose background changes as home grows farther away
a lunch tin that opens onto the smell of the same kitchen each morning
a voice message replayed in a local bell at dusk
a seed from home that turns toward the next crossing
a worn ticket that gains a fresh punch before each opening
a chalk outline that matches a familiar doorstep down to the cracks
competing_duty: bring a lost resident to the one gathering where they can speak for their family
witness a housing claim before the oldest resident leaves for good
escort a new friend to a reunion they are afraid to attend
trade a useful craft lesson for the shelter a household already gave you
deliver a sack of homebound letters from earlier arrivals
help a neighborhood mark a new route before the old one vanishes
carry a community's reply to an invitation across a closed border
stand beside your host when their neighbors question their decision to take you in

1: your ordinary belongings draw an unexpected crowd
a harmless greeting puts your name on a public roster
an ally invites you to supper and asks what you left behind
a local uses a familiar phrase with an entirely different meaning
2: a favor for your host falls at the same hour as a lead about home
two gatekeepers offer access under incompatible promises
someone from home sends a reply that arrives halfway through a local ceremony
another traveler asks to share the next crossing
3: a council proposes closing the crossings while displaced people still depend on them
your remaining route home has room for fewer travelers than are counting on it
a coalition offers passage if the party lets it set the terms for future arrivals
admitting how you arrived could remove an ally's right to shelter travelers
4: the last negotiable crossing opens and both worlds send people asking to be heard
choose which community keeps the only key to the crossing and what it owes the other side
a crossing can stay open for everyone if the party accepts a lifelong obligation to both sides
several families have one final chance to cross before the route is sealed for a generation

cliches: the first person you meet explains the whole world
the outsiders are important because a prophecy says so
home stops mattering once the adventure begins
everyone who crossed wants the same thing
the way back depends on a randomly discovered relic
